headline: 14 killed as bus crashes into truck in Natore
summary: A head-on collision between a Chapainawabganj-bound bus and a sand-laden truck left 14 dead and 32 injured, including five traders from Shariatpur.
details: A head-on collision between a Chapainawabganj-bound RP Special Transport bus and a sand-laden truck occurred early Tuesday morning on the Natore-Pabna highway near the Bonpara police investigation center in Boroigram, Natore.
At least 14 people were killed in the crash, with 32 others injured. Nine victims died on the spot, while five others passed away after being taken to various hospitals.
Among the victims were five traders from Shariatpur's Jazira upazila who were traveling to Bagmara to purchase agricultural seeds and other products.
The tragedy struck a family from Patuakhali; a father and his 8-year-old daughter died, while the mother and 10-year-old son are currently fighting for their lives in the hospital.
The mother, a senior official at Pubali Bank, remains unaware that her husband and daughter have passed away as she receives treatment for her injuries.
The victims from Shariatpur include Jewel Madbor, Salal Molla, Sohag Shikdar, Abdus Samad Fakir, and Shahin Bepari, all of whom from the seorangy area of Jazira.
The bodies of the deceased traders are being transported back to Shariatpur after legal formalities are completed.
According to reports, the bus supervisor was driving the vehicle while the actual driver was sleeping in the back seats.
caption:
14 dead, 32 injured. A family's holiday trip turned into a tragedy in Natore.

A head-on collision between a Chapainawabganj-bound RP Special Transport bus and a sand-laden truck occurred early Tuesday morning on the Natore-Pabna highway near the Bonpara police investigation center in Boroigram, Natore.

At least 14 people were killed in the crash, with 32 others injured. Nine victims died on the spot, while five others passed away after being taken to various hospitals.

Among the victims were five traders from Shariatpur's Jazira upazila who were traveling to Bagmara to purchase agricultural seeds and other products.

The tragedy struck a family from Patuakhali; a father and his 8-year-old daughter died, while the mother and 10-year-old son are currently fighting for their lives in the hospital.

The mother, a senior official at Pubali Bank, remains unaware that her husband and daughter have passed away as she receives treatment for her injuries.

The victims from Shariatpur include Jewel Madbor, Salal Molla, Sohag Shikdar, Abdus Samad Fakir, and Shahin Bepari, all of whom from the seorangy area of Jazira.

The bodies of the deceased traders are being transported back to Shariatpur after legal formalities are completed.

According to reports, the bus supervisor was driving the vehicle while the actual driver was sleeping in the back seats.

headline_marked: Tarique Rahman: [[Government will not interfere in local elections]] like previous regime
headline: Tarique Rahman: Government will not interfere in local elections like previous regime
summary: The BNP Chairman and Prime Minister visited Chittagong, urging party workers to select acceptable candidates for the upcoming local government elections.
details: BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed an organizational meeting at the Radisson Blu Chittagong Bay-View on Tuesday night, where over 450 leaders and workers from the city, North, and South districts were present.

He assured party members that the current government will not interfere in the upcoming local government elections, unlike the previous 'fascist' government, and urged them to unite and select candidates with high public acceptability.
Tarique Rahman emphasized the importance of maintaining law and order, calling on party workers to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and involve respected community members to ensure stability.

He warned that party members must not be involved in any criminal activities, stating there would be no compromise on such behavior, and suggested that active responsibility could reduce crime by 50%.
The Prime Minister also directed workers to remain united against rumors and conspiracies spread by the banned Awami League and Jamaat-e-Islami in the name of the current government.
Prior to the meeting, he visited the JM Sen Hall puja mandap to extend greetings to the Hindu community during the Sharadiya Durga Puja celebrations.
This visit marks a continuation of his engagement with Chittagong, following his first visit to the city on August 9 after taking the oath as Prime Minister.
